intro.p: EXAM RULES – READ CAREFULLY: $•$ Problem 1 A contains 10 true/false questions about various topics covered in the course so far, Problem 1 B contains a short question about national accounts, and Problem 2 contains four parts A,B,C and D about the IS-LM model. This quiz will be graded on a 100-point scale, according to the breakdown specified below. $•$ Please write your answer below each question in the space provided, and do not remove the staple. $•$ Please write your name on every page. $•$ Read the questions carefully and keep your answers short and to the point. Points will be deducted for ambiguous or illegible answers, while partial credit will be assigned in case of a mistake carried over from earlier to later parts of the same problem. $•$ For Problem 1 A, you are not required to explain your answers. Explanations will not be taken into consideration when grading. $•$ You will be asked to draw a graph. Please make sure to always label axes and curves, add arrows to denote shifts in the relevant curves, and mark the axes in the locations corresponding to equilibrium. $•$ By signing below, you agree to comply with the MIT honor code and one additional rule specific to this quiz: No discussing the quiz with anyone until after the quiz. $•$ Good luck!

partes.p: [3 points] The unemployment rate is the ratio of the total number of employed people and the total population.

solucao.p: [3 points] The unemployment rate is the ratio of the total number of employed people and the total population. False: The employment rate is the ratio of employed and labor force.

partes.p: [3 points] All else equal, if two firms merge, GDP does not change.

solucao.p: [3 points] All else equal, if two firms merge, GDP does not change. True.

partes.p: [3 points] At the natural rate of unemployment, the price level equals the expected price level.

solucao.p: [3 points] At the natural rate of unemployment, the price level equals the expected price level.
True.

partes.p: [3 points] If markups rise, then the natural rate of unemployment decreases.

solucao.p: [3 points] All else equal, if markups rise, then the natural rate of unemployment decreases.
False: The natural rate rises.

partes.p: [3 points] In an open market operation the central bank changes the supply of money by buying or selling bonds in the bond market.

solucao.p: [3 points] In an open market operation the central bank changes the supply of money by buying or selling bonds in the bond market.
True.

partes.p: [3 points] The higher the interest rate, the higher the price of a bond today.

solucao.p: [3 points] The higher the interest rate, the higher the price of a bond today.
False: price is lower.

partes.p: [3 points] Consider an economy in which there are two firms, a wheat producer that grows wheat and a bread company that produces bread. In a given year, their respective input costs and sales are:
Wheat producer Bread company Revenue from sales \$300 Revenue from sales \$500 Expenses \$250 Expenses \$450 Wages \$250 Wheat purchases \$250 Wages \$200 d Profits \$50 Profits \$50
In this economy, nominal GDP is \$100.

solucao.p: [3 points] Consider an economy in which there are two firms, a wheat producer that grows wheat and a bread company that produces bread. In a given year, their respective input costs and sales are:
Wheat producer Bread company Revenue from sales \$300 Revenue from sales \$500 Expenses \$250 Expenses \$450 Wages \$250 Wheat purchases \$250 Wages \$200 d Profits \$50 Profits \$50
In this economy, nominal GDP is \$100. False. Using e.g. the sum of incomes, GDP is $250 + 200 + 50 + 50 = 550$.

partes.p: [3 points] The real interest rate is always lower than the nominal interest rate.

solucao.p: [3 points] The real interest rate is always lower than the nominal interest rate. False. Recall the Fisher equation: the real rate equals the nominal rate minus expected inflation. The real rate is lower than the nominal rate if expected inflation is positive, but if expected inflation is negative (i.e. deflation) then the real rate is higher.

partes.p: [3 points] Suppose investment is exogenously fixed. All else equal, if saving increases due to a decline in autonomous consumption, then equilibrium output must decrease.

solucao.p: [3 points] Suppose investment is exogenously fixed. All else equal, if saving increases due to a decline in autonomous consumption, then equilibrium output must decrease. True.

partes.p: [3 points] Consider the Basic IS-LM model where investment, government spending, and taxes are exogenous. If the marginal propensity to consume out of disposable income is 0.5, then a one-unit increase in investment leads to a 2 unit increase in equilibrium output.

solucao.p: [3 points] Consider the Basic IS-LM model where investment is exogenously fixed. If the marginal propensity to consume out of disposable income is 0.5, then the multiplier is 2.0. True.

Money Demand
Assume that the demand for money ($M$), the sum of currency and transaction balances, in the US can be described by
$M = \gamma \cdot (\$Y) \cdot (1 - i)$
where $\$Y$ is nominal GDP, $i$ is the nominal interest rate, and $\gamma$ is a parameter which shifts the money demand curve.

solucao.p: Money Demand
Assume that the demand for money ($MM$), the sum of currency and transaction balances, in the US can be described by
$MM= \gamma \gamma \cdot (\$YY) \cdot (1 -ii)$
where $\$YY$ is nominal GDP, $ii$ is the nominal interest rate, and $\gamma \gamma$ is a parameter which shifts the money demand curve.

partes.p: [4 points] Explain why this demand function depends on $i$, the nominal interest rate, rather than $r$, the real interest rate.

solucao.p: [4 points] Explain why this demand function depends on $ii$, the nominal interest rate, rather than $rr$, the real interest rate. Money demand depends on the nominal interest rate, because this is the opportunity cost of holding money.

How much does output change as a result of this shock to investment? Provide an algebraic answer in terms of the various parameters of the economy. partes.p: [4 points] Building on part 3, if the government wants to ensure output is unchanged from its initial level ($Y_{�}^{*}$) even though investment has declined, how much should it adjust taxes in response to this shock?

solucao.p: [4 points] Building on part 3, if the government wants to ensure output is unchanged from its initial level ($YY_{1}^{*}$) even though investment has declined, how much should it adjust taxes in response to this shock? Using our answer to part 1, taxes need to fall by $\frac{\delta \delta}{cc_{1}}$ to offset the investor caution.

solucao.p: [5 points] Suppose the government increases $tt_{0}$ by one unit. What will be the impact on equilibrium output, Y? Does equilibrium output increase? Explain your answer.

solucao.p: [6 points] Suppose expected inflation rises by one unit. What is the impact of this change on the equilibrium level of investment? What is the effect on the equilibrium level of consumption?
Using the fact that $\frac{dddd}{dd\pi \pi^{ee}} = \frac{bb_{2}}{1-cc_{1}-bb_{1}}$,
For investment: $\frac{dddd}{dd\pi \pi^{ee}} = bb_{1} \frac{dddd}{dd\pi \pi^{ee}} + bb_{2} = bb_{1} \frac{bb_{2}}{1-cc_{1}-bb_{1}} + bb_{2}$.

partes.p: [4 points] Suppose the risk premium $x$ increased by 0.1 units and the nominal interest rate $i$ is equal to 0.01. What problem will the central bank face if it tries to adjust the nominal interest rate $i$ so that this shock has no effect on equilibrium output? Explain briefly why this problem arises.

solucao.p: [4 points] Suppose the risk premium $xx$ increased by 0.1 units and the nominal interest rate $ii$ is equal to 0.01. What problem will the central bank face if it tries to adjust the nominal interest rate $ii$ so that this shock has no effect on equilibrium output? Explain briefly why this problem arises.

The central bank would have to decrease the nominal interest rate by 0.1 to keep output unchanged. The central bank would be hitting the zero lower bound. Nominal interest rates cannot go too far below zero because there is an opportunity cost of buying bonds: holding money which has zero return.
